title: Handover, records and honest compliance claims
audience: Cleaners and supervisors completing a kitchen exhaust handover and its records.
learningOutcomes: Write a handover that states the work done, the access limits and the exclusions.
Refuse to describe the system as compliant or fire-safe.
Keep records that the owner and the competent person can check.

instruction.heading: What a handover is for
instruction.body: A handover is the document that carries the job from the people who did the work to the people who will rely on it. The owner needs it to decide what happens next. The competent person needs it to decide whether a further assessment is needed. The next cleaner needs it to know what is already done and what is not. A good handover is short, specific and limited to what was actually seen and done. A poor handover is long on reassurance and short on facts, and it tends to create the impression that the system has been checked more thoroughly than it has. This lesson teaches you to write a handover that a reader can rely on, because it says exactly what it covers and what it does not.

instruction.heading: The parts of a handover
instruction.body: A handover normally contains the site and location, the date and time, the names of the people who did the work and the people who received the handover, and the scope reference. It then lists the work done, grouped by layer and by location reference, so that the reader can see which accessible surfaces were cleaned and which were not. It states the access limits: sections not seen, panels not opened, areas blocked, and parts outside scope. It lists the exclusions in plain words, such as internal duct, fan internals, fire-suppression components and roof work, where those were not part of the job. It records the observed defects and the escalations, with the times and the people told. It refers to the photographs and their labels, and it identifies the records that go with it. It is signed and dated by the person who prepared it. Each part should be short and precise.

instruction.heading: The language you must not use
instruction.body: Certain words make a claim that the cleaner has no authority to make. Do not write that a system is compliant, certified, fire-safe, passed, approved or inspected in full. Do not write that the fire-suppression system is working, that the duct is clear, or that the fan is safe to run, unless a competent person has said so in writing and the statement is attributed to them. Do not write that the job is complete if any section in the scope was not done. Use exact statements instead: the surfaces cleaned within the written scope, the sections not inspected, the observations made and the limitations that apply. Where the owner wants a sentence for an insurer, a landlord or an authority, the cleaner must not write it. Refer the request to the owner and the competent person, and record that the referral was made.

instruction.heading: Records that the owner and the competent person can check
instruction.body: A record is useful only if another person can check it. Each entry should carry a date, a time, a location reference, the person who made it, and the scope reference. Photographs should be labelled and linked to the entry they support. Escalations and referrals should show who was told and when. Keep the original files and any later amendments, marked with the date and the person making the change, rather than overwriting an earlier entry. Store the records in the approved location for the site.

instruction.heading: Shared duties and the handover
instruction.body: Under the model work health and safety framework, where more than one party has a duty for the same risk, each party keeps its duty and must consult and coordinate with the others. Safe Work Australia's current model code on biological hazards restates this shared-duty approach. The handover is the cleaner's way of meeting that duty in practice. It gives the owner, the competent person and any other duty holder the information they need in a form they can act on. Where the handover shows a gap, send the gap to the people who must close it, and record that you did so.

procedure: Confirm the scope reference and the list of sections covered by the job before writing the handover.
Write the work done, grouped by layer and location reference, using the observations and photographs recorded during the job.
List the access limits and the exclusions, each as a separate line, with the reason and the person told.
List the defects observed and the escalations made, with times and the people told.
Check the wording against the language you must not use. Replace any claim of compliance, safety or full inspection with an exact statement.
Attach the labelled photographs and the related records, and identify the record set by its reference.
Sign and date the handover, have it received by the owner or their delegate, and keep the signed copy in the approved location.

workedExamples.situation: The owner of a hotel kitchen asks you to write, on the handover, that the exhaust system is 'fire-safe and compliant', so that the insurer can be told at renewal. Your scope covered the accessible hood surfaces and the removable filters only.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you write, and what do you refuse to write?
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse to write that the system is fire-safe or compliant. A cleaner's handover covers only the scope and the access the cleaner had, and it cannot make a fire-safety or compliance statement. Write the surfaces cleaned within scope, the sections not inspected or not in scope, the defects observed and the escalations made. Tell the owner that a statement about compliance must come from the competent person, and record the request and the referral.

workedExamples.situation: A handover describes the job as 'complete', but the duct take-off was not accessible and the access panel was taped shut. The owner's file will be read by the next contractor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What changes to the handover, and why?
workedExamples.reasoning: Change 'complete' to a statement of the scope completed and the sections not done. Add the duct take-off as an access limitation, with the panel reference, the reason and the person told. State that the duct beyond the panel was not inspected. The next contractor needs to know what was not seen, so the handover must say so in plain words.

equipmentAndPpe: Handover form with sections for scope, work done, access limits, exclusions, defects, escalations and sign-off.
Labelled photograph log and linked records.
Approved storage location for signed records, with access rules set by the site.
PPE is not usually part of a handover, but the site's rules for documents and photographs apply.

commonErrors.error: Writing 'compliant', 'fire-safe' or 'certified' because the owner has asked for it.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not write it. Write the scope, the access and the limitations, and refer the request to the competent person.

commonErrors.error: Writing 'complete' when a section in scope was not done.
commonErrors.prevention: State the sections completed and the sections not done, and list each limitation separately.

commonErrors.error: Leaving an unseen duct section out of the handover because it was not part of the job.
commonErrors.prevention: List it as an exclusion or access limitation, so the reader can see what the handover does not cover.

commonErrors.error: Overwriting an earlier record when it is corrected.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the original, add the correction with the date and the person making it, and reference the earlier entry.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Under the model WHS framework, duties for the same risk are shared between the parties involved, and each party must consult and coordinate with the others. Safe Work Australia's model code on biological hazards restates this approach. This lesson does not confirm how any particular state applies the framework to kitchen exhaust work.
Confirm both before any record is discarded.

A cleaner's handover is not a certificate, a compliance statement or a fire-safety assessment. Only a competent person, eligible under the requirements that apply, may make such a statement. Writing one without that eligibility is outside this lesson.
This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

qualityStandard: The handover in the worked example states the scope, the work done, the access limits, the exclusions, the defects and the escalations, and contains no compliance, fire-safety or completeness claim not supported by the record.
Each access limitation is listed separately with its reason and the person told.
Each record is dated, located, attributed and linked to its photographs, and corrections are added rather than overwritten.
documentationEvidence: Signed handover with scope reference, work done, access limits, exclusions, defects, escalations and sign-off.
Labelled photograph log linked to the handover.
Referral record for any request for a compliance or fire-safety statement.
Record of the owner or delegate who received the handover.
summary: A handover states the work done, the access limits and the exclusions, in plain words.
Never describe the system as compliant, certified, fire-safe or fully inspected.
Refer any request for a compliance statement to the competent person, and record the referral.
Keep records that a reader can check, with dates, locations, attribution and linked photographs.

knowledgeChecks.question: After a hood clean, the client asks for a fire-safe certificate. What is correct?
options: Write the certificate, because the hood was cleaned and the work was done to a good standard on the day for the client
Decline to write a certificate or fire-safe statement, state the scope and limits, and refer the request to the competent person
Write that the system is fire-safe, but only for the hood, since the hood is the part the cleaner worked on today

knowledgeChecks.question: How should an unaccessed duct section be recorded in the handover?
options: Left out, because it was not part of the work that was booked for the day
Listed as an access limitation or exclusion, with the reason and the person told
Recorded as clean, because it was not visibly dirty from the access point

knowledgeChecks.question: What makes a record useful to an owner and a competent person?
options: It is short, uses reassuring words and avoids listing any limits, so the owner stays calm and happy
It is dated, located, attributed, linked to its photographs, and corrections are added rather than overwritten
It is written by the most senior person on site, whatever the scope of the work booked and the time taken
